subject.title: [Feature]: Add $EDITOR compose mode in TUI (external editor handoff) for multiline prompts

question: Should `openclaw tui` add an external-editor compose flow, and what trigger plus temp-file/process boundary should it use?
rationale: The implementation shape is clear, but the feature launches a user-selected local process and stores prompt text in a temporary file, so maintainer intent is needed for the security posture and user-facing trigger before code work starts.

options.title: Approve a guarded core TUI flow
options.body: Implement the handoff in `src/tui` with explicit user trigger, private temp-file handling, no auto-submit, clear errors, cleanup, docs, and focused TUI tests.

options.title: Defer to broader composer UX
options.body: Keep this open as product backlog until maintainers decide it together with multiline, modal, and vi-mode composer requests.

options.title: Decline external editor in core
options.body: Close the direction after explaining that core TUI will keep in-place composition only and that the existing agent-session editor binding is a different surface.

recommendation.title: Approve a guarded core TUI flow
recommendation.body: Implement the handoff in `src/tui` with explicit user trigger, private temp-file handling, no auto-submit, clear errors, cleanup, docs, and focused TUI tests.

likelyOwner.reason: He already mapped this issue to the TUI code path and called out the same UX/security decision boundary.
